Whoa, sorry! It's IT speak.

Redundant Array of Inexpensive Disks, originally.

They changed the third word to Independent a bit later, so it didn't sound so cheap. :)

Basically a way of doing blockchain before blockchain.

Split the data up into multiple pieces, and scatter it across the disks, with redundancy -- so, if any one disk dies, all the data is still there and a blank disk can be added and "worked back in".

The one I liked the best was RAID-5 and its derivatives; you could have multiple "hot spares" and even "cold spares" (i.e., drives you had purchased but hadn't installed yet) -- so that a data center could withstand 20 drives failing all at once, and never lose a byte of data.

The blockchain, well, changes things.
